newsitem.title: USA: FedEx to add temporary 2 pct surcharge.
newsitem.headline: FedEx to add temporary 2 pct surcharge.

text.p: Federal Express Corp said on Thursday it would add a temporary two percent surcharge to all express package shipments beacuse of high fuel prices.
The surcharge will be delayed until February 3, 1997, after the peak shipping season, the company said.
"Fuel prices have remained stubbornly high and have significantly affected our operating costs," said Alan Graf, president and chief financial officer.

He said jet fuel prices are about 20 percent higher than last year's second quarter and represent a 10 percent increase from the first quarter. The increase in jet and vehicle fuel prices added about $25 million, year-over-year, to the quarter's operating expense, Graf said.

The surcharge will apply to shipments tendered within the United States with certain limited exceptions. It will also apply to all U.S. export shipments, except those to the People's Republic of China and Hong Kong.
The company posted second-quarter earnings of $103.7 million, or $0.90 per share, compared to net income of $89.9 million, or $0.78 per share in last year's second quarter.
